standard_prerequisites.use: The cotangent triangle lemma and its smooth case (Morphisms, triangle-differentials and triangle-differentials-smooth) and the characterization of etale maps as smooth with vanishing differentials; cited inputs with the two-step argument written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Recall etale means smooth with vanishing sheaf of differentials.
Use the triangle lemma to identify Omega_{X_2/S_2} with Omega_{X_2/S_1}.
Use the smooth triangle lemma to conclude f^*Omega_{X_1/S_1} -> Omega_{X_2/S_1} is an isomorphism.
Combine the two identifications to obtain the isomorphism c_f.

proof_roadmap.step: Identify Omega_{X_2/S_2} with Omega_{X_2/S_1} via the vanishing of the etale base differentials.
Conclude the pullback isomorphism from the smooth triangle lemma.

difficulty_reason: In a commutative diagram where both X_2 -> X_1 and S_2 -> S_1 are etale, the comparison map c_f from f^* of the sheaf of differentials to the sheaf of differentials of the base changed diagram is an isomorphism. The proof is a written two-step argument through the cotangent triangle: etale maps are smooth with vanishing differentials, the triangle lemma gives Omega_{X_2/S_2} = Omega_{X_2/S_1}, and the smooth triangle lemma gives that f^*Omega_{X_1/S_1} -> Omega_{X_2/S_1} is an isomorphism. Retained author proof at lines 2020-2029.
